column1: # ci-unit-weights.tsv — the MEASURED cost of each verification unit, in seconds.
# WHAT THIS IS FOR. `ci-units.sh` packs units into shards longest-first, so it
# needs a cost per unit. Nothing here changes WHAT is verified; it changes only
# how the work is distributed, and a wrong number costs wall-clock balance and
# nothing else. That is why this is dated data with provenance rather than a
# EVERY ROW IS FROM ONE RUN: the job logs of run 34945072758 (engine-self-verify
# run #216), a full sharded pass on `ubuntu-latest` at `d2664cdb`, 2026-09-15.
# COVERAGE, AND ITS DATE. That run measured 137 units against an inventory of
# 137 — no gaps, nothing falling back to DEFAULT_WEIGHT. Then main moved the
# same afternoon (0e9f5fcf, two new hooks) and the inventory became 138. The
# one row that measurement could not contain is
# `scripts/hooks/left-off.test.sh`, and it is below with its own provenance:
# measured locally at 120.4 s, TWICE the 60 s the packer would have assumed.
# That is worth reading twice, because it is this file's whole thesis
# happening in real time. A unit landed, was packed at a number nobody had
# checked, and the drift report named it with its replacement row inside two
# Coverage is therefore a CLAIM WITH A DATE, exactly like every number here.
# It was complete at d2664cdb and it will go incomplete again at the next
# suite anyone adds. What is now guaranteed is not that it is complete — it is
# that it SAYS SO when it is not.
#   137 units, 7723 s serial. The largest, and they are what set the
# WHY THIS REBUILD WAS NOT OPTIONAL, AND WHAT IT COST WHILE IT WAS WRONG.
# The previous version of this file predated the workspace-spec suites, so
# THIRTY-TWO of the inventory's 137 units carried no row and were packed at
# FORTY-SEVEN TIMES the weight the packer gave it. The packer therefore put it
# in a shard with eleven other units, and that shard was the wall clock of
#     run #211  shard 12  3185 s        run #213  shard 12  3167 s
#     run #212  shard 12  3262 s        run #216  shard 12  3146 s
# measured with `gh api .../runs/<id>/jobs`. Every other shard in those runs
# finished in 194-1015 s. That is the whole of the "53.9 minutes per push"
# finding, and none of it was a slow test getting slower — it was one correct
# THE FLOOR IS NOW HONEST AND IT IS NOT THE PACKING. 2811.7 s is the largest
# INDIVISIBLE unit, so no shard count can put the wall clock below it while
# that suite is one unit. With these weights the packer isolates it and the
# other 136 units spread across the remaining shards; the wall clock becomes
# that unit rather than that unit PLUS eleven strangers. Making CI faster than
# ~47 min therefore means sectioning that suite (as
# contract-integrity.test.sh is sectioned), not re-tuning this file.
# A WEIGHT THAT IS WRONG NOW REPORTS ITSELF. This file went stale silently and
# stayed stale for days because reading a run's durations back out was manual
# work nobody was assigned. `ci-shard.sh` now compares each unit's measured
# duration against the weight it was planned at and prints a WEIGHT-DRIFT line
# naming the replacement row; `ci-receipts.py verify --weights` does the same
# over the whole run and writes a ready-to-commit file. Re-measuring is now
# THE HISTORY OF THIS FILE IS THE ARGUMENT FOR RE-MEASURING IT. It has been
# rebuilt four times and every version was honestly wrong when it aged:
#   a macOS `--only` sweep       put WTI at 1500.1 s, taken at load average 34
#   the quiet-Mac record         had the same harness at 599 s (2026-09-04)
#   run 34423889101's receipts   said 870.7 s, on the runner
#   run 34434314424's receipts   said 381.6 s, after mutant concurrency landed
#   run 34945072758's job logs   says 402.9 s, and covers the whole inventory
# Five numbers for one harness, none of them wrong when taken. A weight is a
# measurement with a date, never a fact.
# A UNIT WITH NO ROW HERE IS NOT FREE. `ci-units.sh` gives it DEFAULT_WEIGHT and
# packs it as if it were average — never zero. That fallback is correct and it
# is also what hid the 47x error, which is why the drift report above exists.
# HOW TO RE-MEASURE: the coverage job runs
# rows and uploads `ci-unit-weights.measured.tsv` as an artifact. Download it,
# replace the rows below, update the run id in this header. The plan changes;
# Section SCR now only checks that scratch-reaper.test.sh is discovered and that every threshold
# the reaper needs is declared; the reaper's suite and its 53-mutant pass run as their own unit.
# The old 676.8 s (a contended full suite, when SCR still ran them) planned it past the merge
# gate's 600 s cap. Measured alone at 4e73fd89: "PASS 4.8s", ci-shard 1/1 unit(s) passed; the
# merge of that commit measured it at 9.0 s beside 62 other checks.
# Behavioral half under ci-shard.sh after its land-lock home moved into the fixture
# (693528de, "After: PASS 172.4s, ci-shard 1/1 unit(s) passed"); the mutation pass
# runs only at the nightly's workspace-mutants gate and is not in this number.
